title: How to Make a Whiskey Sour That Actually Tastes Right
subtitle: Bright, balanced, and built with real citrus.
summary:
The Whiskey Sour is one of those drinks that gets a bad reputation because it’s so often done wrong. Too sweet, too artificial, or built from a mix that tastes nothing like real citrus. I avoided ordering them for a long time because of that.

But when it’s done properly—with fresh lemon juice, a clean whiskey, and just enough sweetness—it’s one of the most balanced drinks you can make. It’s bright, smooth, and just structured enough to feel like a real cocktail instead of something thrown together.

quick_mix.headline: Quick Mix
lines: Shake with ice, strain into a rocks glass

editorial_sections.title: Why Most Whiskey Sours Miss the Mark
editorial_sections.body:
The biggest problem is shortcuts. Bottled sour mix might be easy, but it strips the drink of everything that makes it work. You lose the brightness, the balance, and that clean edge that fresh citrus brings.

Once you switch to real lemon juice, the entire drink changes.

editorial_sections.title: Balance Is Everything
editorial_sections.body:
A good Whiskey Sour is all about balance between sour and sweet. Too much lemon and it feels sharp. Too much sugar and it turns flat.

I usually start with a 3/4 oz lemon and 1/2 oz simple syrup, then adjust slightly depending on the whiskey.

editorial_sections.title: To Egg White or Not
editorial_sections.body:
The egg white version adds texture more than flavor. It softens the edges and gives the drink a smooth, almost creamy finish.

I’ll use it when I want the drink to feel more polished, but it’s completely optional.

editorial_sections.title: What a Good Whiskey Sour Should Feel Like
editorial_sections.body:
It should feel bright from the first sip, with the whiskey still clearly present underneath. The citrus should lift the drink, not overpower it.

When it’s right, it’s one of the easiest drinks to go back to.

steps: Add whiskey, lemon juice, simple syrup, and egg white (if using) to a shaker.
Dry shake (no ice) if using egg white.
Add ice and shake until well chilled.
Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice or serve up.
Optional: garnish with a cherry or lemon peel.
notes: Always use fresh lemon juice. Adjust sweetness slightly depending on your whiskey and taste preference.
